I help my neighbors, who are mostly elderly, with their home computers. It really bothers me the way appliance stores exploit the elderly when it comes to computers. They always con them into buying far more than they need or can handle, often based on some nerdy kid salesman's own gamer-based biases. And they always push Windows like it's the only option. Windows really sucks for the elderly novice user. It's user interface is hopelessly over-modal, inconsistent in behavior and design, and poor at representing the state of the machine and content of its file system. It's like a Swiss army knife --it does everything and none of it well. It over-idiot-proofs an architecture that is over-complicated to begin with and that just results in a machine that seems, to old folks, to act in random incomprehensible ways. Old folks seem to universally have trouble grasping the concept of its file structure or the distinctions between applications on the OS and things on the Web. They always misplace things because they can't navigate the file system. There's too much crap for them to keep track of. Too many abstract concepts taken for granted. I keep telling them to do some homework, figure out exactly what they really need before they buy, and go with Mac or Android (even just settle for a tablet, if all they need is some word processing, email, and messaging) so they can have simpler user interfaces they can more readily understand.
